plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 (Ge/ZnS dual-band filter on CaF2) based on prior iteration results showing best_target_score=0.8679 with 9 valid candidates. Feedback directives specify tighter thickness bounds [80,400] nm and reduced optimizer step size to prevent thickness overshoot. Four complementary routes proposed: (1) direct implementation of feedback with refined bounds, (2) asymmetric cavity topology for improved dual-band separation, (3) alternative ZnSe/ZnS material pair for index contrast comparison, (4) reduced 20-layer count for manufacturability. All routes maintain parent_route_id='route_02' per refinement_chain instruction. Repaired evidence ID typo in route_02_reduced_layers and research_influence.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Dual-Band Filter with Constricted Thickness Bounds [80-400 nm]
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Constricting thickness initialization bounds to [80, 400] nm and reducing optimizer step size by 50% will prevent thickness overshoot observed in prior iteration, forcing the solver to optimize around resonant quarter-wave thicknesses and improve convergence toward the theoretical dual-band transmission limit.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack with dual-cavity resonance for two distinct passbands. Ge (high index ~4.0) and ZnS (low index ~2.2) provide sufficient index contrast for sharp spectral edges within 24-layer constraint.
routes.proposed_topology: 22 explicit layers: Air | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | CaF2 substrate

routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer Ge/ZnS multilayer filter on CaF2 substrate for dual-band transmission. Wavelength bands: transmit 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm; block 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm. All 22 layer thicknesses are optimization variables with bounds [80, 400] nm. Initialize thicknesses at quarter-wave values (Ge ~205 nm, ZnS ~375 nm at 3300 nm reference). Use gradient-based and differential evolution optimizers with step size reduced by 50% from standard defaults. Evaluate coherent TMM across 2500-5000 nm spectrum. Score candidates by mean transmittance in passbands and blocking bands. No metal layers. Air incidence, unpolarized light. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Direct implementation of feedback directives: constricted thickness bounds to [80, 400] nm and reduced optimizer step size by 50% to prevent thickness overshoot observed in iteration_06 where some layers exceeded 490 nm.

routes.title: Ge/ZnS Asymmetric Dual-Cavity Filter for Improved Band Separation
routes.scientific_hypothesis: An asymmetric cavity design with different spacer thicknesses for the two passbands will improve spectral separation between methane (3.3 μm) and CO2 (4.25 μm) bands compared to symmetric quarter-wave initialization, reducing passband coupling and improving blocking in the 3.35-4.20 μm transition region.
routes.design_principle: Dual-cavity bandpass filter with asymmetric spacer layers tuned to each target wavelength. First cavity optimized for 3300 nm, second cavity for 4250 nm, with distributed Bragg reflectors between cavities.
routes.proposed_topology: 22 explicit layers: Air | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | Ge(spacer1) | [ZnS/Ge]_3 | ZnS(spacer2) | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | Ge | CaF2 substrate with explicit thickness for each layer
design_variables: All 22 layer thicknesses optimized within [80, 400] nm bounds
Spacer layer thicknesses initialized asymmetrically: spacer1 ~205 nm for 3300 nm, spacer2 ~260 nm for 4250 nm

routes.title: ZnSe/ZnS Dual-Band Filter Alternative Material Pair
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing Ge with ZnSe (n~2.4-2.6 in IR) will provide lower absorption loss in the 3-5 μm range while maintaining sufficient index contrast with ZnS (n~2.2), potentially improving passband transmittance at the cost of reduced blocking steepness due to lower index contrast.
routes.design_principle: Same 22-layer dual-cavity topology as route_02 but with ZnSe substituting for Ge. Lower index contrast (ZnSe/ZnS ~1.2 vs Ge/ZnS ~1.8) traded for reduced material absorption in mid-IR.
routes.proposed_topology: 22 explicit layers: Air | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | ZnSe | ZnS | CaF2 substrate

routes.design_principle: Same Ge/ZnS dual-cavity topology as iteration_06 but with 20 layers instead of 22, removing one Ge/ZnS pair from each end of the stack to reduce total thickness while preserving cavity structure.
